subtopics.title: The Atmosphere — Composition, Structure and Heating

questions.question: The two most abundant gases in the atmosphere, in order, are:
options: Oxygen at 78 per cent, then nitrogen at 21 per cent
Nitrogen at 78 per cent, then oxygen at 21 per cent
Carbon dioxide, then oxygen
Water vapour, then nitrogen

questions.question: Temperature rises with height in the stratosphere because:
options: It is closer to the sun than the troposphere
Meteors burn up there and release heat
The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet radiation and warms the surrounding air
Greenhouse gases are concentrated there

questions.question: The atmosphere is heated from below means:
options: Volcanic heat from the crust warms the air
The core conducts heat through the crust into the air
Sunlight only shines upward from the horizon
The surface absorbs shortwave insolation and re-radiates longwave energy that warms the air above it

questions.question: Heat carried sideways by wind from one region to another is called:
options: Advection
Conduction
Radiation
Convection

subtopics.title: Moisture, Clouds and the Three Rainfall Types

questions.question: Relative humidity is:
options: The mass of vapour in a cubic metre of air
The temperature at which condensation begins
The vapour in the air as a percentage of the maximum that air at that temperature could hold
The rate at which water evaporates from a dam

questions.question: Dew point is the temperature at which:
options: Air becomes saturated and relative humidity reaches 100 per cent
Frost always forms regardless of moisture
Rain must start falling
Evaporation exceeds condensation

questions.question: Afternoon thunderstorms on the Highveld in summer are the classic South African example of:
options: Frontal rainfall
Orographic rainfall
Rain shadow drizzle
Convectional rainfall

questions.question: The Little Karoo is dry largely because it:
options: Lies in the rain shadow on the leeward side of the Cape mountain ranges
Is too far from the equator for rain
Sits at too high an altitude for clouds
Receives only frontal rain in summer

subtopics.title: The Restless Crust — Plates, Folds, Faults and Quakes

questions.question: Compared with continental crust, oceanic crust is:
options: Thicker and lighter
Thinner and denser
Made mostly of granite
Always older

questions.question: At a convergent boundary where an ocean plate meets a continental plate:
options: The plates slide past each other without landforms
A mid-ocean ridge forms between them
The denser ocean plate subducts, melts, and feeds volcanoes like those of the Andes
Both plates rise to form a rift valley

questions.question: In folded rock, the upfold and downfold are called, in order:
options: Horst and graben
Syncline and anticline
Scarp and dip
Anticline and syncline

questions.question: The Richter and Mercalli scales differ in that:
options: Richter measures energy released as one value per quake; Mercalli measures observed intensity, which varies from place to place
Both measure damage but in different countries
Mercalli is measured by instruments; Richter by observers
Richter applies only to volcanic eruptions

subtopics.title: Mapwork Essentials — Scale, Contours, Gradient and the Synoptic Chart

questions.question: On a 1:50 000 topographic map, 2 centimetres on the map represents:
options: 500 metres on the ground
1 kilometre on the ground
2 kilometres on the ground
50 kilometres on the ground

questions.question: Where contour lines cross a river valley, they form a V that points:
options: Downstream, away from the source
Toward magnetic north
Upstream, into the higher ground
Toward the sea

questions.question: Two points differ by 200 metres in height and lie 4 000 metres apart. The gradient is:
options: 1 in 4
1 in 40
1 in 20

questions.question: As a cold front passes over Cape Town, the weather changes to:
options: A temperature drop, wind swinging south-westerly, rising pressure and showers
Warmer air, northerly wind and falling pressure
Clear skies and calm winds immediately
A heatwave with berg winds

subtopics.title: The Pot on the Stove — Air, Heat and Rain Made Simple

questions.question: Mountaintops are cold although they are nearer the sun because:
options: The sun avoids high ground
The atmosphere is heated from below, and summits are further from the warmed surface air
Snow blocks incoming radiation
Wind removes all heat at altitude

questions.question: The three lifts that force air to rise and make rain are:
options: Gravity, tides and rotation
Evaporation, transpiration and condensation
Hot ground convection, mountain barriers, and cold fronts wedging under warm air
Ozone, carbon dioxide and water vapour

questions.question: Blanket against sunscreen distinguishes:
options: Cloud cover from fog
Dew from frost
Convection from advection
Greenhouse gases trapping outgoing heat from the ozone layer blocking incoming ultraviolet

subtopics.title: The Cracked Eggshell — Plates, Folds and Faults Made Simple

questions.question: In the eggshell picture, the jostling of the shell pieces is driven by:
options: Slow convection currents in the mantle dragging the plates
The moon's gravity pulling the crust
Ocean waves pushing the continents
Earthquakes shaking the plates loose

questions.question: The East African Rift Valley is best described as:
options: Two continents colliding and crumpling
A fold mountain range being squeezed upward
A widening trench where the continent is pulling apart between faults
A chain of subduction volcanoes

questions.question: The Cape Fold Mountains formed when:
options: A volcano built them layer by layer
Rock layers were slowly squeezed and buckled into folds around 300 million years ago
A rift valley dropped between two faults
Glaciers carved them from a plateau

questions.question: The epicentre of an earthquake is:
options: The underground point where the rock snaps
The instrument that records the shaking
The zone that feels no shaking at all
The point on the surface directly above the focus

subtopics.title: The Bathtub Rings — Mapwork Rehearsed Out Loud

questions.question: In the bathtub picture, tightly packed rings on the toy mountain mean:
options: A steep slope, because height changes quickly over a short distance
A gentle slope, because the water drained slowly
A river crossing the slope
Flat land at the summit

questions.question: The spoken gradient routine is:
options: Multiply the two heights and halve the answer
Add height difference to distance and divide by two
Find the height difference, convert the map distance with the scale, divide distance by height, and state it as 1 in the answer
Count the contour lines and multiply by the scale

questions.question: On a station model, temperature and dew point sitting close together warn that:
options: A berg wind is blowing
The air is nearly saturated and rain is close
The station's instruments are faulty
Pressure is about to rise sharply

questions.question: The feathers on a station model's wind shaft show:
options: Cloud cover in eighths
The chance of rain as a percentage
Air pressure in hectopascals
Wind speed in knots
